propositions: LLMConfig must expose a headers field with dict[str, str] type defaulting to empty dict to allow operators to attach custom request headers for gateway labeling without displacing credentials.

Headers must resolve with three-layer precedence (CLI -c llm.headers > REBAR_LLM_HEADERS env var > [tool.rebar.llm] file table), raising LLMConfigError on malformed JSON in any layer rather than silently degrading.

The ${env:VAR} placeholder grammar must resolve from environment at config time with unset variables raising LLMConfigError, while ${run:KEY} placeholders must remain unresolved but validated against a closed vocabulary (trace_id, ticket_id, operation) at config time.

Header name and value validation must reject reserved names (authorization, x-api-key, cookie, host, proxy-authorization case-insensitive), non-RFC-7230-token name characters, and CR/LF/NUL in resolved values, with denylist errors directing to llm.api_key as the supported auth channel.

Validation must run after ${env:VAR} substitution to detect injected control characters in resolved values, preventing a configured ${env:GATEWAY_TAG} with value foo\r\nInjected: bar from bypassing header injection checks.

$$ must escape to a literal $ anywhere in a value, so $${VAR} yields ${VAR} unsubstituted and unrecognized placeholders (${foo:bar}, ${envVAR}, unclosed ${...}) must raise LLMConfigError rather than being accepted as literals.
